_meta.description: Curated public interest-incidence rates for Constanza's audience layer (app/services/constanza_audience.py). Deliberately small — every entry needs an actual cited source; an interest phrase that doesn't map to one of these returns 'unsupported_trait' rather than an invented rate. See the Phase 2 plan doc.
_meta.policy: No rate ships without a source + source_date. Extend by adding entries here, not by asking the LLM to estimate a rate.

categories.label: Sports fan (general)
categories.source: Gallup, 'As Industry Grows, Percentage of U.S. Sports Fans Steady' (June 2015 poll): 59% of Americans say they are sports fans — one point below Gallup's average since 2000; 66% of men and 51% of women
categories.sample_scope: US adults, general population. This is a 2015 poll — older than the other rate here; Gallup describes the share as steady over time, so it is used as published. Upper-income households run higher (68%); that subgroup is not modeled.

categories.label: Plays video games
categories.source: Entertainment Software Association (ESA), 'Essential Facts About the U.S. Video Game Industry' 2026 (released June 2026): 53% of men and 46% of women actively playing video games. 'all' is the population-weighted mean of those two (~49%); the report's 67% headline covers ages 5-90 and is not comparable
categories.sample_scope: Share of men / of women who play (the report's headline is 67% of Americans ages 5-90 playing weekly, which includes children). Age-band rates aren't modeled in v1 — ESA reports the gender skew reverses for older cohorts (Boomer women 52% vs men 47%) — so the flat gender rate is applied across all ages.
